summary: The 1972 Federation Cup was the tenth edition of the premier women's international team tennis competition, with 31 nations competing at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, South Africa, from 20–25 March. South Africa beat Great Britain in the final, earning their first title. It was the first final without the United States or Australia, and South Africa became the first other team to win the Fed Cup.
one_line: South Africa won the 1972 Federation Cup in Johannesburg, beating Great Britain in the first final without the United States or Australia.
key_facts: The 1972 Federation Cup was the tenth edition of the most important competition between national teams in women's tennis.
31 nations participated in the 1972 Federation Cup.
The 1972 tournament was held at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, South Africa.
The 1972 Federation Cup took place from 20–25 March.
South Africa defeated Great Britain in the 1972 final.
The 1972 final was the first final not featuring United States or Australia.
The 1972 victory gave South Africa their first Federation Cup title.
South Africa became the first team other than United States or Australia to win the Fed Cup.
